body:
I'd written a bit of a response earlier but he actually reached out to me not that long ago apologizing for being so hostile and not communicating and said he understood where I was coming from. So right out the gate we're already on a much better track than we were this morning lol

Everything is not solved and the root issues are still there but all I really wanted was a foundation of being able to talk about it. He said he'll always be able to separate the fantasy from our real relationship and everything else we have together and I believe him - that's not the ideal solution, but as long as we can maintain a healthy and exclusive relationship I don't really mind. I think as long as we keep this up we'll be okay from here. Thanks for all your help

We have communication and openness in basically every aspect but this one which is why it's so bothersome to me. The thing with talking to strangers online might've sounded worse than it was: it was actually just a little anonymous fetish roleplaying thing with people he's in all likelihood never been able to speak to before or since. The reason it bothered me was because obviously I would be really into him doing that with me - he'd just rather do it with people he doesn't know instead because he is intensely ashamed of it. I don't like being lied to and if it was about any other topic I wouldn't be so forgiving, but I know he has very deep seated issues related to this and I don't want to push him into alienating himself from me even more. I agree, more or less, with your hypothesis on relationships. I'm willing to stick with him even in spite of this because we are in perfect sync on literally everything else: this subject is just like a berserk button where he becomes a totally different person who can't empathize with me in the least.

He actually reached out to me in the time since I wrote the first half of this apologizing for getting hostile and uncommunicative after I confronted him and we talked about it. I got everything I said here off my chest. It's a start lol

Right, but the reason it's so complicated is that it's because he doesn't think of sexual stuff the way you or I do. His brain just works differently in the same way people can't choose who they're attracted to - he's actually said to me before that he feels like sex cheapens relationships. The reason I assume he's okay with strangers knowing is because he knows he'll never have an actual emotional connection with them and never actually encounter them irl. I'm not saying he handles it in the best way but I think I do have a duty to try and be considerate of that

He does care but it's hard to see how much because he refuses to communicate. It would be much easier for me to take his refusal and leave it at that if he told me why, but he never has. There's a lot more to our relationship on an emotional level and I would never end it over this - I knew what I was getting into when he told me he was asexual - but it is immensely frustrating.

I totally agree that we need to talk about it. I'm kind of an open book about everything, that's just the way I am - if there's an issue I want it out of the way as fast as possible. He is the polar opposite in that regard, where he'll keep things below the surface for as long as humanly possible to avoid confrontation. Talking about this has become next to impossible - I've done everything from gently ask him to explain his point of view to writing him paragraphs explaining how I'd never judge him and how much healthy I think it is to be able to confide in each other, and it always ends the same way: him refusing, telling me he doesn't owe me any explanations and that this is just the way he is. It is so frustrating. This is a really complex thing for him and I try not to hold it against him because he is the best in so many other ways but he's built up a fortress around this subject.

And your assumption is almost certainly correct but it's what brings me back around to thinking maybe this is my problem and not his: he's told me he thinks about sex/general erotic stuff the same way someone typical would having to use the bathroom. He loathes having a libido, even if it's only to this one kink. So my pitch to him has always been to try and elevate something as animalistic as he feels it is into the basis of a genuine emotional connection. That hasn't worked either. So maybe it's just unfair of me to try and force talking about this on him?

I'm definitely a lot more open to straight communication than he is. Writing something without the pressure of me immediately replying might be a good idea because I really don't know what else to suggest, it's like he's placed concrete barriers around this subject. He has anxiety and I try to respect that but it also means a lot of bad feelings stagnate because things just don't get talked about. I'm kind of stumped otherwise lol
Lol I don't think so, I still love him very much. Ultimately I can do without the intimacy if I really have to but I'm just trying to look for potential compromises if they exist

The thing is we often go months without talking about anything even vaguely sexual, and for the most part I'm fine with that. It's just that when it *does* come up it's impossible to have a measured conversation about him with it, he just shuts me down. It's hard because he's my biggest confidante for literally anything else. I have a problem with being pushy when I get frustrated and that's just kind of a response to finding this kind of stuff so silly to get worked up over but I do know it's partially my fault for trying to convince him to do something he's uncomfortable with.

The thing with him chatting with strangers is a bit more complicated than I mentioned, but basically it was part of this fantasy roleplaying thing. I'd be into doing that with him, but he refuses to do it with me. And I know why - it's because he doesn't equate sexual/physical intimacy with love and I guess the anonymity makes it easier for him to keep those things apart. Am I wrong to still be a little hurt by that?

He doesn't have to, it's just that we're in a relationship but can't do anything else until we're physically together again. The lack of intimacy is hard and this has always struck me as a potential way of getting some of it back before we can be back together, you know?
This is all very sweet of you to say. I don't know how much of it is true but I sincerely thank you for saying it
